items.title: Bill Holman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 13, 1999
items.q: I’m trying to find some of the things that I wrote for Charlie Barnet for those two albums we did.

ctx.x: Who were your favorites when you were listening to the radio? Let’s say, oh 1940 and you were about 13?

Oh, there were a lot. I always liked Basie’s band, Benny Goodman, I was starting to get into Woody Herman, Charlie Barnet and of course Duke. I didn’t understand Duke though, it was a little deep for me. Basie’s old band, you know with Prez and all those guys, it was right out there. And I never lost a love for that feel, you know that really radical swinging that the Basie band did that at time. It had a small band feel almost.
Curious you used the word “radical.” Why would you say radical swinging?

items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: Snader Telescription in which the title number is played by Charlie Barnet and His Orchestra, including Claude Williamson, piano, Bill Holman, tenor sax...

ctx.x: Oh, a whole bunch -- well, let's see, Billy Byers, Bill Holman, and -- well, they did the majority of them. And of course there's a montage there that was really a collection of parts out of different arrangements, you know. Andy Gibson, William Moore, Jr., and Billy May. And then there's -- let's see, there's, "Jeeps Blues," on there, the original Ellington arrangement, with Willy Smith doing it this time. And Clarke Terry does his Mumbles with the big band.
Gee, that would be great to see and hear here.
